job.title: ASP5 - Finance Analyst
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a chance for a high-performing Finance Analyst to contribute to high-quality financial reporting, governance, and analysis in a fast-paced environment where your work directly supports informed decision-making.

About the Role
You will support the financial reporting and policy function, contributing to accurate, timely reporting and strong financial governance outcomes. The role will work closely with internal stakeholders and external assurance bodies to meet Commonwealth reporting obligations and drive continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide financial analysis and advice to support business outcomes
  • Support financial policies, procedures and governance frameworks
  • Coordinate audit activities, including managing information requests and supporting documentation
  • Apply relevant accounting standards, legislation and Commonwealth financial frameworks
  • Prepare reports, briefings and written responses for stakeholders
About You:

  • Understanding of Commonwealth financial frameworks (including PGPA) and Australian Accounting Standards
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail
  • Confident communicator with the ability to build relationships across diverse stakeholders

Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.

Locations
Adelaide SA, Canberra ACT, Sydney NSW

Apply Now

job.title: APS6 Financial Analyst
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an APS6 Financial Analyst to join a collaborative finance team supporting one of Australia's most significant national capability programs.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid-career finance professional seeking exposure to complex government financial management, compliance, assurance and reporting within a high-profile and evolving environment.

About the Role
As an APS6 Financial Analyst, you will provide financial assurance, compliance and policy advice to stakeholders while supporting effective stewardship of public resources. You will work across a range of financial systems, reporting tools and governance frameworks to ensure compliance with relevant legislation, accounting standards and whole-of-government requirements.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Delivering financial compliance and assurance activities through data analysis, reporting and evidence-based recommendations
  • Managing key financial management functions including travel, corporate credit cards and expenditure commitments
  • Developing and maintaining financial policies, procedures and user guidance materials
  • Supporting financial literacy initiatives and compliance awareness programs
  • Providing advice to stakeholders on financial policy and governance requirements
  • Contributing to financial reporting, assurance reviews and continuous improvement activities
  • Building strong relationships across the organisation to support informed decision-making
About You To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Experience in financial analysis, compliance, assurance or financial management
  • Understanding of, or the ability to quickly acquire knowledge of, the Commonwealth Resource Management Framework and PGPA environment
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret financial information and identify risks
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Proven ability to build productive relationships with diverse stakeholders
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • High attention to detail and a commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality work
  • A collaborative and professional approach to supporting team and organisational outcomes
What's on Offer
This is a unique opportunity to contribute to a nationally significant program while developing your career within a supportive and professional environment. You will gain valuable exposure to government financial management, assurance frameworks, policy development and stakeholder engagement while working alongside experienced finance professionals.

If you are looking for a challenging and rewarding APS6 opportunity where your analytical skills can make a genuine impact, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Work Health & Safety Advisor
job.description:
About the Team
The role sits within the agency's People and Culture function and works closely with employees, managers, Health and Safety Representatives (HSRs), and senior leaders across the organisation.
The team is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving workplace health and safety policies, programs, governance processes, and best practices. Their focus is on creating a workplace where employees feel physically and psychologically safe and supported.

About the Role
The agency is seeking an experienced Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) professional to provide expert advice and support across a large and diverse workforce. This role is responsible for helping create a safe, healthy, and positive workplace by identifying risks, supporting managers and employees, investigating incidents, and ensuring compliance with workplace safety legislation and policies.
The successful candidate will play a key role in driving safety initiatives, improving safety systems and processes, and promoting a strong safety culture across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead and coordinate key workplace health and safety initiatives and projects.
  • Provide expert WHS advice to managers and employees on complex workplace matters.
  • Conduct risk assessments and support the identification and management of workplace hazards.
  • Investigate incidents and workplace safety concerns and develop corrective actions.
  • Maintain and monitor risk registers, safety records, and reporting frameworks.
  • Support compliance with workplace health and safety legislation, policies, and procedures.
  • Develop and improve WHS policies, procedures, training materials, and guidance documents.
  • Analyse safety data and prepare reports, briefing papers, and governance documentation.
  • Work closely with stakeholders to promote a strong safety culture and continuous improvement.
  • Support regulatory responses, audits, and assurance activities where required.

Must Have
 
  • Experience in a WHS advisory, safety, risk, compliance, or injury management role.
  • Strong knowledge of workplace health and safety legislation and best practice principles.
  • Experience conducting incident investigations and risk assessments.
  • Experience identifying and managing physical and psychosocial workplace risks.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Experience preparing reports, briefings, recommendations, and safety documentation.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Experience working within a government, regulatory, corporate, or highly governed environment.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12- Month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • Rate: $60.26 hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

job.title: Business Compliance Officer
job.description:
Business Compliance Officer – Newcastle $49.22 per hour + superannuation | 7-Month Contract | Newcastle CBD

Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Business Compliance Officer to join a major water utility organisation based in Newcastle.

This is an excellent opportunity for a compliance professional with strong stakeholder management skills to contribute to environmental compliance, customer engagement and operational risk management across essential water and wastewater services.

This contract is available for an immediate start and will run through to 30th June 2027.

About the Role Working within the Business Customers team, you will support compliance activities relating to trade wastewater, tankered waste and recycled water customers.

The position combines operational compliance, investigations, stakeholder engagement and administrative reporting to ensure customers meet their regulatory and contractual obligations.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing operational compliance activities associated with tankered trade waste and recycled water services.

  • Investigating non-compliance issues and recommending appropriate corrective actions.

  • Coordinating tanker access to wastewater treatment facilities and supporting compliance audits.

  • Monitoring customer agreements, risk management plans and regulatory requirements.

  • Building and maintaining positive relationships with commercial customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Managing reporting, invoicing and billing reconciliation through internal systems.

  • Supporting inspection programs, regulatory reporting and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Providing advice and assistance to customers regarding compliance requirements.

About You We are looking for a well-organised and proactive professional who can confidently manage compliance requirements while maintaining strong customer relationships.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Tertiary qualifications in business, engineering or equivalent relevant experience.

  • Experience in compliance, regulatory services, environmental management, utilities or a related field.

  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills.

  • Demonstrated ability to investigate issues, solve problems and manage competing priorities.

  • Excellent written communication, reporting and administrative skills.

  • Strong computer literacy and attention to detail.

  • Ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.

Experience in water utilities, wastewater management, environmental compliance or customer-facing regulatory roles will be highly regarded.

What's on Offer?
  • $49.22 per hour + superannuation.

  • 7-month labour hire assignment, concluding 30th June 2027.

  • Newcastle CBD location – Honeysuckle.

  • Immediate commencement available.

  • Opportunity to work with an established essential services organisation.

  • Varied role combining compliance, customer engagement and operational activities.

Apply Now If you have a background in compliance, environmental services, utilities or regulatory operations and enjoy working with a diverse range of stakeholders, we'd love to hear from you.

Click Apply Now and submit your current resume.

For a confidential discussion, contact:

Mark Seery
Senior Recruitment Consultant
Chandler Macleod
0437 356 484

Please note: The successful candidate will be required to complete a criminal background check as part of the pre-employment process.

job.title: Wheel Dozer Grader Operator
job.description:
Wheel Dozer / Grader Operators FIFO from Perth | $65.00 per Hour | Immediate Starts Available
Our client is seeking experienced Wheel Dozer and Grader Operators for upcoming opportunities on a large-scale Pilbara mining operation. These positions offer the opportunity to work within a high-performing production mining environment, with immediate interview availability and upcoming mobilisation dates.
What's on Offer
  • $65.00 per hour
  • FIFO from Perth
  • Immediate interview availability
  • Immediate starts available
  • 8 Days On / 6 Days Off, 7 Nights On / 7 Nights Off roster
  • Tuesday-to-Tuesday roster
  • Opportunity to work with a leading Pilbara mining operation
  • Potential for repeat fixed-term opportunities for proven performers
  • Potential ongoing labour hire opportunities for high-performing candidates
About the Role Successful candidates will be responsible for operating Wheel Dozers and/or Graders in a production mining environment while maintaining safe and efficient site operations.
Duties may include:
  • Maintaining haul roads and pit infrastructure
  • Dump and working area maintenance
  • Road construction and upkeep
  • Supporting safe production outcomes across active mining areas
  • Working effectively around autonomous haulage operations
Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 2 years' experience operating Wheel Dozers and/or Graders within a large-scale production mining environment
  • Demonstrated ability to safely and efficiently perform production mining activities
  • Experience maintaining haul roads, dumps, working areas, and pit infrastructure
  • Previous experience working around Autonomous Haulage Systems (AHS)
  • FrontRunner experience highly regarded
  • Current C Class Manual Driver's Licence
  • Strong safety focus and reliable operating history
  • Recent operating experience, with time away from the role not exceeding 6 months
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment medical and drug & alcohol screening
About You You are a safety-focused operator with strong production mining experience and a proven ability to work within a high-performing team. You take pride in maintaining high operating standards and contributing to safe and productive site outcomes.
Please note this opportunity is suited to experienced production mining operators. Candidates with entry-level skills or limited exposure to the required equipment may not meet the minimum project requirements.
Apply Now If you have recent production mining experience operating Wheel Dozers and/or Graders and are looking for your next FIFO opportunity, we would like to hear from you.
Submit your current resume outlining your equipment history, recent operating experience, and mining background.
Shortlisting is underway and suitable candidates will be contacted regarding interviews, mobilisation requirements, and upcoming start dates.

job.title: Advisor Survey Delivery
job.description:
Advisor Survey Delivery
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto in Perth, Western Australia
  • 12-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
 
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders. Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Advisor Survey Delivery.  

Based in Central Park offices with the opportunity for ad hoc travel, this role offers the chance join a supportive team focused on safety, collaboration and delivering operational excellence within a leading global organisation, where you will be contributing to key operational and business outcomes.

Reporting to the Superintendent – Survey Delivery, you'll use your skills and experience to support business priorities, collaborate with key stakeholders and contribute to the success of the operation.

In this role, you will:  
  • Lead the delivery of biological surveys in remote areas of the Pilbara, with a strong focus on safety.
  • Plan and coordinate survey activities, including health and safety requirements, scheduling, site mobilisation and logistics for environmental consultants.
  • Apply Rio Tinto’s contractor management processes to support safe and effective survey delivery.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of survey delivery processes, including planning, coordination and field logistics.
  • Forecast accommodation requirements for the Biological Assessments team
  • Coordinate aviation requirements for helicopter-supported biological surveys, including engagement with aviation providers and operational readiness.
About You
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Practical problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to think on your feet and make sound decisions.
  • Interest in native flora and fauna and environmental approvals for Rio Tinto Iron Ore operations through the delivery of biological surveys in the Pilbara.
  • Experience using technical software, such as GIS or ArcGIS.
  • Dedication to everyone's safety.
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing.
 
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia's most experienced workforce partners. You'll receive a competitive hourly pay range paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.
 
Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading mining operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Diversity & Inclusion
Everyone is welcome at Chandler Macleod. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and inclusive teams. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, females, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and members of the LGBTIQA+ community. Together, we're creating workplaces where people feel they belong, can be themselves and have the opportunity to thrive.

job.title: Senior Employee Relations Consultant Level 6 | State Government | Perth WA
job.description:
Senior Employee Relations Consultant (Level 6) | State Government | Perth WA
Lead complex workplace relations matters and influence positive organisational outcomes within a high-profile Western Australian Government department.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Employee Relations Consultant (Level 6) to provide specialist advice and strategic employee relations support across a diverse and complex workforce.
Key Responsibilities
As the Senior Employee Relations Consultant, you will:
  • Provide expert advice and consultancy services to managers and employees on complex employee relations matters, including:
    • Grievances and complaints
    • Disciplinary processes
    • Misconduct and behavioural matters
    • Performance management
    • Workplace investigations
  • Manage complex employee relations cases from initial assessment through to resolution, ensuring procedural fairness and compliance with relevant policies and legislation.
  • Advise senior executives, managers, and executive leadership on options and strategies for resolving sensitive workplace issues.
  • Conduct reviews, assessments, and investigations relating to employee relations matters.
  • Coach and support HR practitioners and leaders in managing difficult workplace situations.
  • Interpret and apply relevant employment legislation, industrial instruments, policies, procedures, and government standards.
  • Develop, review, and maintain employee relations policies, procedures, and guidance materials.

job.title: Work Health & Safety Advisor
job.description:
About the Team
The role sits within the agency's People and Culture function and works closely with employees, managers, Health and Safety Representatives (HSRs), and senior leaders across the organisation.
The team is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving workplace health and safety policies, programs, governance processes, and best practices. Their focus is on creating a workplace where employees feel physically and psychologically safe and supported.

About the Role
The agency is seeking an experienced Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) professional to provide expert advice and support across a large and diverse workforce. This role is responsible for helping create a safe, healthy, and positive workplace by identifying risks, supporting managers and employees, investigating incidents, and ensuring compliance with workplace safety legislation and policies.
The successful candidate will play a key role in driving safety initiatives, improving safety systems and processes, and promoting a strong safety culture across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead and coordinate key workplace health and safety initiatives and projects.
  • Provide expert WHS advice to managers and employees on complex workplace matters.
  • Conduct risk assessments and support the identification and management of workplace hazards.
  • Investigate incidents and workplace safety concerns and develop corrective actions.
  • Maintain and monitor risk registers, safety records, and reporting frameworks.
  • Support compliance with workplace health and safety legislation, policies, and procedures.
  • Develop and improve WHS policies, procedures, training materials, and guidance documents.
  • Analyse safety data and prepare reports, briefing papers, and governance documentation.
  • Work closely with stakeholders to promote a strong safety culture and continuous improvement.
  • Support regulatory responses, audits, and assurance activities where required.

Must Have
 
  • Experience in a WHS advisory, safety, risk, compliance, or injury management role.
  • Strong knowledge of workplace health and safety legislation and best practice principles.
  • Experience conducting incident investigations and risk assessments.
  • Experience identifying and managing physical and psychosocial workplace risks.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Experience preparing reports, briefings, recommendations, and safety documentation.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Experience working within a government, regulatory, corporate, or highly governed environment.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12- Month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • Rate: $60.26 hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Our client is a not-for-profit, values-driven community services organisation, seeking an experienced Administration/Finance Officer to join their team based in Capalaba and to oversee payroll, bookkeeping, reporting and office operations.


About the role.

You will manage a mix of bookkeeping, payroll, reporting and general administration responsibilities, contributing to well-run operations and strong internal support.


Key responsibilities.

Finance
- Payroll, PAYE, BAS and superannuation payments 
- Internet banking (accounts receivable and payable) 
- Monitor expenditure and assist with budget preparation 
- Monthly and annual financial reporting 
- Liaise with auditors 
- Rental contribution recording (e.g., Centrepay) 
- Petty cash, banking, and administration of emergency relief
 
Administration
- Purchase and maintain supplies (stationery, food packs, household goods) 
- Maintain asset, key, and staff training registers 
- General correspondence and administrative coordination 
- Liaise with relevant external bodies/stakeholders as required 
- Assist with coordination of AGM administration
 
Teamwork & continuous improvement
- Attend and minute monthly team meetings 
- Contribute to policies/procedures, continuous improvement and strategic planning 
- Maintain positive working relationships across the team


About you.

You’re an experienced Finance professional who is looking for a flexible opportunity to work 30 hours a week, without needing to cancel your additional commitments outside of work.

You take pride in keeping systems, compliance and day-to-day operations running smoothly.

You bring relevant tertiary qualifications in Administration and/or Finance, along with strong, practical capability across bookkeeping, payroll and financial reporting.

job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced SAP / Technology Strategic Sourcing Lead to join a high-performing procurement function on a 12-month contract.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a senior procurement professional with deep expertise in technology sourcing, SAP commercial negotiations, System Integrator engagements, and strategic vendor management. You will play a key role in leading complex sourcing initiatives, driving commercial outcomes, and partnering with senior stakeholders across major technology programs.

About the Role As the SAP / Technology Strategic Sourcing Lead, you will lead end-to-end procurement activities across enterprise technology portfolios, supporting critical business and transformation initiatives.

You will be responsible for developing sourcing strategies, leading complex commercial negotiations, managing supplier relationships, and delivering best-value outcomes while ensuring compliance with procurement governance frameworks.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead strategic sourcing activities across SAP, technology, software, cloud, and professional services categories.
  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies for high-value and complex procurement initiatives.
  • Manage commercial negotiations with SAP vendors, System Integrators, and technology service providers.
  • Deliver procurement outcomes that balance value, risk, and operational requirements.
  • Build strong relationships with executive stakeholders and project teams.
  • Support major transformation and technology programs through effective procurement leadership.
  • Ensure procurement activities meet governance, compliance, and policy requirements.
About You To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Extensive experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or category management within technology environments.
  • Proven experience negotiating SAP agreements, software licensing contracts, and technology services arrangements.
  • Strong understanding of System Integrator engagements and large-scale technology procurement programs.
  • Demonstrated success delivering complex commercial and procurement outcomes.
  • Exceptional stakeholder management, influencing, and negotiation skills.
  • The ability to think strategically while remaining hands-on in delivery.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Our client, a leading organisation in its field, is looking for an experienced Financial Accountant to join their team ASAP in a temporary, full-time capacity based on-site in Brisbane’s Northern Suburbs.


Key Responsibilities & Skills
  • Perform balance sheet reconciliation
  • Assist with year-end audit preparation
  • Update and maintain accounting schedules, including:
    • Lease accounting (AASB 16)
    • Prepayments
    • Accruals
  • Complete bank reconciliations
  • Provide support to the Finance Manager as required
  • Assist with month-end and year-end close activities
  • Strong Excel capability
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge

About You
  • High attention to detail and strong numerical accuracy
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • CA/CPA qualified or studying
  • Available to work on-site in Brisbane’s Northern Suburbs
  • You will be working closely with the CFO, they are looking for somebody that can hit the ground running

How to Apply

If you’re an accounting professional looking for a temporary opportunity, with the potential for an extension, in Brisbane’s northside, apply now with your resume.


ASAP Start!

Chandler Macleod is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourages applications from all backgrounds.

job.title: Communications and Engagement Officer
job.description:
About the role
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Communications and Engagement Officer to join a busy Project Management Office on a 12-month contract. This role will play an important part in supporting communications and stakeholder engagement for major infrastructure and capital works projects, including the Ballina Bridges Duplication Project.

Working closely with project teams, contractors, local businesses and the wider community, you will help deliver clear, consistent and engaging communications while providing administrative and project coordination support.

This opportunity is offering full time hours, with flexible working arrangements available, including a 9-day fortnight or 4-day working week. 


Duties
  • Develop and implement communication and community engagement strategies for major infrastructure projects.
  • Coordinate community information sessions and stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Prepare project updates, newsletters, flyers, correspondence and other public-facing communications.
  • Engage with residents, businesses, contractors and key stakeholders to provide updates, gather feedback and address concerns.
  • Manage stakeholder databases, analyse feedback and prepare engagement reports.
  • Coordinate digital communications across social media, websites and email marketing platforms.
  • Provide administrative and project coordination support, including scheduling, reporting and progress tracking.
  • Monitor project compliance and maintain accurate project documentation and records.
  • Work collaboratively with project teams and the Communications team to ensure consistent messaging.

Skills and Experience
  • Qualifications in community engagement, communications, project management or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience in communications and/or community engagement, ideally within construction, civil engineering or major infrastructure projects.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build relationships and engage with a range of stakeholders.
  • Highly organised with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong computer literacy, including Microsoft 365 and corporate software systems.
  • Experience with digital communication channels, including social media, content management systems and email marketing platforms.
  • Familiarity with mapping software and graphic design capabilities.
  • Willingness to provide administrative support to project management teams.
  • Current Class C driver's licence.

Benefits
  • 12-month contract opportunity.
  • Full-time hours with a flexible 9-day fortnight or 4-day working week arrangement.
  • Salary negotiable based on experience and suitability.

How to apply
Sound interesting? We would love to hear from you! Click APPLY NOW to upload a copy of your current resume, or call Jo Ellerman on 02 6691 9105 for a confidential discussion.
job.salary: Salary negotiable based off skills & experience

job.title: Data Developer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for experienced Data Developers to support a major data transformation initiative. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the migration of enterprise reporting and analytics capabilities to Snowflake and Power BI while working within a large and complex government environment.

With multiple positions available across Australia, you will play a key role in developing, optimising and supporting modern data and reporting solutions that drive business performance and decision-making.

About the Role As an Data Developer, you will support the transition of reporting products from an existing analytics environment into Snowflake and Power BI. You will work closely with business stakeholders, project teams and technical specialists to deliver scalable, high-performing reporting and data solutions.

You will act as a subject matter expert across Snowflake, SQL and Power BI while contributing to platform governance, optimisation, troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Administer, configure and manage Snowflake environments
  • Support data warehouse migration and transformation activities
  • Analyse business requirements and develop scalable data solutions
  • Optimise and tune complex SQL code to improve performance
  • Develop and support enterprise reporting solutions using Power BI
  • Implement and maintain governance controls, security roles and data management practices
  • Troubleshoot complex technical and platform-related issues
  • Monitor platform performance, capacity, compliance and service health
  • Conduct data quality assurance, testing and validation activities
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders, ICT teams and data consumers
  • Develop technical documentation, standards and support materials
  • Mentor and support team members across Snowflake, Power BI and SQL capabilities
  • Manage workflow requests and support activities through JIRA
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Strong hands-on experience with Snowflake, including data modelling, ETL/ELT processes and performance optimisation
  • Advanced SQL development skills, including troubleshooting and query optimisation
  • Strong Power BI experience, including data modelling, dashboard development, DAX and visualisation best practices
  • Experience working with SAS, including analysis and code translation
  • Knowledge of data migration, warehousing and transformation projects
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical capabilities
  • Experience supporting users, stakeholders and technical teams
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Ability to work effectively in complex and evolving environments
Highly Desirable
  • Professional certification in Data Analytics or Business Analytics
  • Experience working within an Australian Government ICT environment
  • Experience supporting large-scale enterprise reporting or data transformation programs
  • Understanding of data governance, privacy and compliance frameworks
Benefits
  • 12-month contract opportunity with potential extension
  • $61.86/Hourly + Super
  • Multiple locations available: Geelong, VIC; Surry Hills, NSW; Newcastle, NSW; Adelaide, SA; Brisbane, QLD
Eligibility:
Australian Citizenship is mandatory for this opportunity. If you are an experienced Data Developer with strong expertise across Snowflake, Power BI, SQL and enterprise data transformation, we encourage you to apply today.

Applications close: Wednesday 25 November 2026.


At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Labourers - Expression of Interest
job.description:
Labourers - Expression of Interest
Location: Canberra, ACT (Various Depot Locations Across Canberra)
Pay Rate: $43.82 per hour + Super
Employment Type: Casual Opportunities

Expression of Interest - Canberra Labourers
Chandler Macleod is seeking expressions of interest from motivated and reliable Labourers to join our talent pool for upcoming opportunities with a respected government sector client in Canberra.

These hands-on outdoor roles offer the opportunity to contribute to the presentation and maintenance of Canberra's public spaces, helping keep parks, recreational areas, shopping precincts, and community facilities safe, clean, and attractive for residents and visitors.

If you enjoy physical outdoor work, take pride in delivering quality outcomes, and thrive working both independently and within a team, we'd love to hear from you.

Typical Duties Successful candidates may be required to:
  • Perform general labouring, grounds maintenance, and cleaning duties.
  • Maintain parks, open spaces, sporting fields, recreational facilities, and community areas.
  • Undertake mowing, weeding, pruning, litter collection, and leaf removal.
  • Clean public amenities, including toilet facilities and public spaces.
  • Operate horticultural equipment, machinery, and vehicles safely and effectively.
  • Conduct pre-start checks and basic maintenance on equipment and vehicles.
  • Assist with tree maintenance, weed control, and landscaping activities.
  • Follow established safety procedures and operational requirements.
  • Maintain a strong commitment to workplace health and safety.

About You To be considered for future opportunities, you will ideally have:
  • Previous labouring, landscaping, horticulture, grounds maintenance, cleaning, or outdoor work experience.
  • A strong commitment to workplace safety.
  • The ability to work effectively both independently and within a team.
  • Good communication and customer service skills.
  • Basic digital literacy and confidence using mobile devices.
  • Reliability, initiative, and a strong work ethic.
  • The physical fitness required for manual outdoor work in varying weather conditions.

Essential Requirements
  • Permanent Residency or Australian Citizenship.
  • Current C-Class Driver's Licence.
  • White Card (Construction Induction).
  • Asbestos Awareness Card.
  • Ability to meet the physical demands of the role.
  • Flexibility to work from various depot locations across Canberra.

Desirable Qualifications
  • Temporary Traffic Management (TTM) qualification or willingness to obtain.
  • Medium Rigid (MR) Driver's Licence or higher.
  • Experience operating horticultural equipment and machinery.
  • Ability to read and interpret safety documentation, traffic management plans, and operating procedures.

Why Register Your Interest?
  • Competitive pay rate of $43.82 per hour plus Super.
  • Opportunities to work outdoors and stay active.
  • Potential for ongoing casual assignments.
  • Experience working with a respected government sector client.
  • Supportive team environment and future career opportunities.

Register Your Interest If you have experience in labouring, grounds maintenance, landscaping, horticulture, cleaning, or related outdoor work, we'd like to hear from you.

Submit your application today to join our Labourer Talent Pool and be considered for upcoming opportunities across Canberra.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Service Guidance Lead
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for experienced Service Guidance Officers to join a high-performing team responsible for developing and maintaining participant-focused guidance and resources.

This is an exciting opportunity for professionals with strong writing, stakeholder engagement, research, and policy interpretation skills who can translate complex information into clear, accessible guidance that supports positive outcomes.

Location: Newcastle NSW, Geelong VIC, Richmond VIC, or Adelaide SA
Contract: 12-Month Labour Hire Contract
Start: ASAP

About the Role:
As a Service Guidance Officer, you will play a key role in developing, reviewing, and maintaining internal and external guidance materials. Working within a collaborative environment, you will ensure resources are evidence-based, accessible, and aligned with organisational policy positions while keeping participant needs at the centre of all deliverables.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders, subject matter experts, and external representatives to deliver high-quality guidance products and support continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the development, review, and maintenance of participant-focused guidance and resources.
  • Translate complex policy, operational, and technical information into clear, plain English content.
  • Research and analyse information from multiple sources to ensure guidance materials are evidence-based and accurate.
  • Engage with stakeholders to gather insights and feedback that improve guidance products.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and advice on guidance-related matters.
  • Represent the branch in cross-functional and multidisciplinary projects.
  • Support responses to executive, ministerial, and government requests.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, products, and service delivery.
  • Manage competing priorities while maintaining high standards of quality and accuracy.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience writing clear, concise, and user-friendly resources.
  • Strong ability to translate complex information into plain English.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Proven research, analysis, and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to quality outcomes.
  • Ability to work independently with limited direction.
  • Adaptability and resilience in changing environments.
  • A collaborative approach and commitment to professional standards and governance requirements.


If you meet the above criteria and are interested in this role please - APPLY now

job.title: Front of House Engagement Officers
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with the Australian National Maritime Museum to find enthusiastic, confident and people-focused Casual Front of House Engagement Officers to join our Visitor Engagement team in Pyrmont. 

This is not a role where you will spend your day behind the scenes. You will be right at the heart of the Museum experience. 

From the moment visitors arrive, you will help set the tone for their day. You will welcome people from across Australia and around the world, help them find their way, answer questions, support admissions and attractions, and make sure every visitor feels welcome. 

If you genuinely enjoy people, bring energy to a team and take pride in delivering great service, this could be the perfect summer role for you. 

WORK SOMEWHERE A LITTLE DIFFERENT 

The Australian National Maritime Museum brings Australia's maritime stories to life through extraordinary exhibitions, historic vessels, collections and experiences. Set on Sydney's waterfront, the Museum is a place for discovery, learning, connection and adventure. 

Our Front of House team is a big part of what makes that experience memorable. 

THE ROLE

$34.96 PER HOUR + SUPER 

Every day will be different. 

You will work across admissions, exhibitions, attractions and public spaces, helping create an environment that is welcoming, safe, engaging and enjoyable. 

  • Welcoming visitors with warmth, confidence and enthusiasm 
  • Delivering friendly, informed and genuinely helpful customer service 
  • Processing admissions, scanning tickets and operating ticketing and point-of-sale systems 
  • Checking tickets, wristbands and access credentials for exhibitions and attractions 
  • Helping visitors with enquiries, directions and wayfinding 
  • Managing the cloakroom and supporting smooth visitor flow 
  • Keeing an eye on public spaces and helping maintain a safe and welcoming environment 
  • Talking with visitors about the Museum and identifying opportunities to promote Museum memberships 
  • Working alongside a great team to deliver an outstanding visitor experience.
Most importantly, you will help make people feel welcome from the moment they arrive. 

WHY JOIN US? 

This is more than a casual customer service role. It is an opportunity to work somewhere iconic, meet people from all walks of life and be part of the energy of the Museum during its busiest season. 

WHAT'S ON OFFER? 

  • Casual work across the busy summer period, including school holidays 
  • Potential opportunities for extension, depending on operational requirements 
  • A unique workplace on Sydney's waterfront 
  • A welcoming, collaborative and people-focused team 
  • The opportunity to build experience in visitor engagement, customer service and cultural attractions 
  • A role where your energy, attitude and interaction with visitors genuinely matter. 
WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

PEOPLE WHO LIKE PEOPLE. 

You do not need to know everything about maritime history. What matters is that you are approachable, reliable, curious and confident engaging with people from different backgrounds. 

YOU'LL BRING

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills 
  • A warm, friendly and proactive approach to customer service 
  • Confidence engaging with a diverse range of visitors 
  • Reliability, initiative and sound judgement 
  • Flexibility and the ability to adapt when priorities change 
  • Good attention to detail 
  • Confidence using computer systems and processing transactions 
  • A team-first attitude and willingness to jump in and help. 
EVEN BETTER IF YOU HAVE 

  • Experience in visitor services, attractions, hospitality, customer service, ticketing or retail 
  • Experience using point-of-sale systems 
  • Additional language skills, particularly Mandarin or Korean. 
WHAT YOU'LL NEED 

  • A current NSW Working with Children Check 
  • Availability to work a minimum of three days per week 
  • Availability to work Saturday or Sunday, with Saturday availability particularly important to supporting Museum operations. 
READY TO COME ABOARD?

APPLICATIONS CLOSE AT 11:59PM AEDT ON SUNDAY 22 NOVEMBER 2026.

Click APPLY and send us your resume and a short cover letter responding to the selection criteria. 

AND YES, REAL PEOPLE WILL READ YOUR APPLICATION 

Museum employees review applications, so do not give us a generic response. Tell us about you. Tell us why you would be great with our visitors. Tell us what you would bring to the team. 

We genuinely value the time and thought you put into your application, so use the opportunity to help us get to know you. 

Australian citizenship is not required for these positions, as successful candidates will be engaged through a labour hire arrangement. 

WANT TO KNOW MORE? 

Contact Gary Ward at Chandler Macleod on 02 7245 5361, or Shane Hodges at the Museum on 02 8241 8303.

job.title: Data Analyst
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Data Analyst to support a major enterprise data transformation initiative. This opportunity offers the chance to work within a high-performing analytics and reporting team, delivering insights that support operational performance, workforce planning and continuous improvement across a large government environment.

About the Role

As a Data Analyst, you will play a key role in supporting the transition to a modern data platform and enterprise reporting environment. You will work closely with project stakeholders to analyse data, develop reporting solutions and provide actionable insights that support strategic decision-making.

Key Responsibilities
  • Analyse complex datasets to identify trends, insights and performance outcomes
  • Develop and maintain reports, dashboards and visualisations using Power BI
  • Extract, transform and validate data using Snowflake, SQL and SAS
  • Support data quality assurance, testing and validation activities
  • Prepare reports, presentations and briefing materials for stakeholders
  • Assist with governance and operational reporting activities
  • Support project delivery, planning and progress reporting
  • Respond to stakeholder enquiries and reporting requests
  • Monitor and manage workflow requests through JIRA
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and business projects
About You
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Strong experience working with Snowflake, including data modelling and ETL/ELT processes
  • Advanced Power BI skills including dashboard development, DAX and data visualisation
  • Strong SQL capability with experience writing and optimising complex queries
  • Experience using SAS for analysis and code translation
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Experience delivering reporting and insights in complex environments
  • Ability to engage effectively with business and technical stakeholders
  • Strong attention to detail with a focus on data quality and accuracy
Highly Desirable
  • Professional certification in Data Analytics or Business Analytics
  • Experience working within an Australian Government ICT environment
  • Exposure to enterprise data transformation or reporting projects

Benefits

  • 12-month contract opportunity with potential extension
  • $61.86/Hourly + Super
  • Multiple locations available: Geelong, VIC; Surry Hills, NSW; Newcastle, NSW; Adelaide, SA; Brisbane, QLD
Eligibility:
Australian Citizenship is mandatory for this opportunity. If you are an experienced Data Analyst with strong Snowflake, Power BI, SQL and SAS expertise, we encourage you to apply today.

Applications close: Wednesday 25 November 2026.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

job.title: Major Projects Sourcing Lead – Manager Level
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Engineering / Major Projects Sourcing Lead to join a high-performing procurement team. This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic procurement professional with significant experience delivering sourcing outcomes across major engineering, infrastructure, capital works, or complex project environments.

This role will suit a commercially astute procurement leader who can balance strategic thinking with hands-on delivery while building strong relationships across senior stakeholder groups.

About the Role Reporting to senior leadership, you will be responsible for leading complex sourcing initiatives and procurement activities that support major projects and operational objectives. You will provide strategic procurement expertise, drive commercial outcomes, and engage with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead end-to-end sourcing activities for complex engineering and major project requirements.
  • Develop and implement strategic sourcing strategies that deliver value and mitigate risk.
  • Manage supplier engagement, tender processes, and commercial negotiations.
  • Build trusted relationships with internal stakeholders and project teams.
  • Identify opportunities for cost optimisation, process improvement, and supply chain efficiencies.
  • Ensure procurement activities comply with relevant governance and policy requirements.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Extensive experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or category management.
  • Proven experience supporting major projects, engineering, infrastructure, or capital works programs.
  • Strong commercial acumen with demonstrated negotiation and contract management expertise.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and influencing skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a complex and fast-paced environment.
  • Experience working within Federal Government or State Government procurement environments.

job.title: Senior Project Manager
job.description:
Senior Project Manager - Building Projects (12-Month Assignment)
Location: Perth, WA
Reporting to: Principal Project Manager

Lead Landmark Public Infrastructure Projects Across Western Australia

An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Senior Project Manager to join a high-performing team delivering significant non-residential building projects on behalf of the Western Australian Government.
Working within the General Agencies team of the Buildings and Contracts business unit, you will lead the delivery of multiple construction projects valued up to $20 million while providing leadership and oversight to a small team of project professionals.
This is a unique opportunity to influence the successful delivery of projects that directly benefit Western Australian communities and public services.

About the Role
As Senior Project Manager, you will lead a team of three and be responsible for the planning, management and successful delivery of a portfolio of building projects. In addition to your leadership responsibilities, you will act as the lead project manager on one or more major projects, requiring a practical, hands-on approach throughout the project lifecycle.
You will work closely with client agencies, consultants, contractors and key stakeholders to ensure projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to the highest quality standards.

Typical Projects

Projects delivered by the General Agencies team include:
  • Perth Zoo Café and Function Centre and Primate Run
  • Sam Kerr Football Centre
  • HBF Park Upgrades
  • Perth Concert Hall Redevelopment
  • Perth Cultural Centre Redevelopment
  • Broome Sobering Up Centre
  • Kulungah Myah Family Centre Upgrade
  • Don Aitken Centre Upgrades for Main Roads WA
Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the delivery of a portfolio of government building projects from initiation through to completion.
  • Manage complex construction projects valued up to $20 million.
  • Provide leadership, mentoring and supervision to project management staff.
  • Manage project scope, budgets, schedules, procurement and contract administration activities.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with client agencies, consultants, contractors and stakeholders.
  • Identify and manage project risks and issues to ensure successful outcomes.
  • Monitor and report on project performance, governance and delivery milestones.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant legislation, policies, standards and procurement requirements.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated project management experience within the building or construction industry.
  • Proven experience delivering medium to large-scale non-residential construction projects.
  • Experience leading and supervising project teams.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Sound knowledge of construction contracts, procurement and project governance.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects.
  • A collaborative leadership style with a hands-on approach to project delivery.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience delivering projects for government, public sector or client-side organisations.
  • Qualifications in Project Management, Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture or a related discipline.
  • Knowledge of Western Australian government procurement and contract management processes.
Why Apply?

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to some of Western Australia's most significant public infrastructure projects while working alongside experienced professionals in a collaborative and outcomes-focused environment.
If you are an accomplished construction project manager who thrives on balancing project delivery with team leadership, we would like to hear from you.

Apply now and help deliver projects that create lasting value for the Western Australian community.

job.title: Service Guidance
job.description:
Assistant Director - Service Guidance Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced  Assistant Director - Service Guidance.

This is an exciting leadership opportunity for a strategic and capable professional to contribute to the delivery of clear, accessible guidance that supports operational excellence and nationally consistent outcomes. The role is responsible for leading complex projects, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and providing expert advice that supports quality service delivery and business outcomes.

As an Assistant Director, you will lead a small team while managing stakeholder relationships across a diverse and complex environment. You will play a key role in developing guidance, supporting business improvement initiatives, and influencing strategic decision-making at senior levels.

Key Responsibilities
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support the development of collaborative service guidance.
  • Provide strategic advice relating to participant pathways, participant cohorts, and business system processes.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across access, planning and operational processes.
  • Identify, manage and escalate risks, issues and emerging priorities through effective reporting and stakeholder engagement.
  • Lead and develop a small team responsible for delivering guidance materials, knowledge articles and communications.
  • Coordinate competing priorities, manage workflows and provide visibility of team capacity and performance against deliverables.
  • Prepare and provide high-quality briefings, reports and advice for senior executives and key decision-makers.
  • Represent the organisation in stakeholder forums and negotiations to achieve positive business outcomes.
  • Contribute to strategic projects and organisational initiatives that support operational effectiveness and service excellence.
About You You are an experienced leader with a demonstrated ability to manage complex work programs, influence stakeholders and deliver high-quality outcomes in fast-paced environments.

You will bring:

  • Strong leadership experience with the ability to coach, mentor and develop staff.
  • Exceptional planning, organisational and prioritisation skills.
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement and relationship management capabilities.
  • Proven ability to influence, negotiate and build consensus across diverse groups.
  • Experience managing complex projects, competing priorities and sensitive issues.
  • Strong analytical and decision-making skills supported by sound judgement.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement and delivering customer-focused outcomes.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience leading teams in a hybrid working environment.
  • Comfortable with new ways of thinking about accessibility and enthusiastic about accessible design & development will be highly regarded
  • Understand how to develop Plain English resources within the government style guide
  • Knowledge of government frameworks, legislative requirements, policy development and decision-making processes.
  • Experience delivering operational guidance, business improvement initiatives or service delivery outcomes within complex organisations.
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to lead meaningful work with national impact.
  • Collaborative and supportive leadership environment.
  • Exposure to complex strategic projects and senior stakeholder engagement.
  • Opportunity to shape service delivery outcomes and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Leadership role with responsibility for developing team capability and performance.
If you're an experienced leader who thrives in complex environments and is passionate about delivering quality outcomes, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Cleaner
job.description:
Cleaner - Brisbane City 

Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Cleaner to join the team in Albert Street, Brisbane CBD. If you take pride in high presentation standards, work well independently, and consistently hit KPIs, we’d like to hear from you.

What’s on offer
  • Full-time position
  • Salary: $58,490 + super
  • High-profile CBD client site:  Albert Street, Brisbane
About the role You’ll be responsible for maintaining a clean, safe, and well-presented site across offices and shared facilities.

Key duties
  • General cleaning duties including vacuuming, mopping, sweeping, and dusting
  • Cleaning and sanitising bathrooms, kitchens, offices, and common areas
  • Emptying bins and disposing of waste appropriately

  • NV1 Clearance (desired)
  • Australian Citizens only 
  • Minimum 1 year cleaning experience
  • Strong communication skills
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Ability to meet performance expectations, including KPI achievement
Apply now If you meet the above requirements and are ready to start, please apply with your resume.

job.title: Haul Truck Operator
job.description:
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced CAT 777 Dump Truck Operator to support day-to-day mining operations in the Gove region, NT.

This is a great opportunity to join a safety-focused team working on site with Rio Tinto. You'll work alongside experienced crews, supporting production targets while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes.

Reporting to the site Supervisor, your responsibilities will include:
  • Operating Caterpillar 777 haul trucks safely and efficiently
  • Conducting pre-starts and routine equipment checks
  • Hauling ore/waste in line with mine plans, procedures and production schedules
  • Reporting hazards, defects, near-misses and incidents promptly
  • Maintaining accurate operational records and supporting a strong safety culture
About You
  • Demonstrated experience operating CAT 777 (or similar mining haul trucks)
  • Previous mine site / production mining experience (highly regarded)
  • Current Australian Driver Licence
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills
  • Dedication to everyone’s safety and following site procedures
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment medical and drug & alcohol testing
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
  • Competitive hourly rates paid weekly
  • Superannuation paid on all hours worked
  • Consistent roster and work-life balance (8/6)
  • Opportunity to gain experience with Rio Tinto
  • Dedicated Chandler Macleod support team
  • Access to future opportunities across Rio Tinto operations
Apply Now!

Ready to take the next step in your mining career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia’s leading operations. We’re recruiting now and encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Diversity & Inclusion Everyone is welcome at Chandler Macleod. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and inclusive teams. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, females, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and members of the LGBTIQA+ community. Together, we're creating workplaces where people feel they belong, can be themselves and have the opportunity to thrive.

job.title: Corporate Compliance Specialist
job.description:
Corporate Compliance Specialist

Brisbane Inner Northern Suburbs - Hybrid Working - 9-Day Fortnight

Our client is a highly regarded organisation operating within a complex and highly regulated environment. Due to continued growth, they are seeking an experienced Corporate Compliance Specialist to take ownership of trade compliance, corporate governance, regulatory reporting and assurance activities across the business.

This is an excellent opportunity for a compliance professional looking to work in a dynamic environment where they can influence business outcomes, mitigate risk and drive continuous improvement. Reporting to a senior leadership team member, you will be responsible for the implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of compliance frameworks, ensuring adherence to Australian and international regulatory requirements.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing trade compliance activities including import/export controls and licensing requirements
  • Providing compliance advice and guidance to key stakeholders across the organisation
  • Conducting internal audits, compliance reviews and assurance activities
  • Maintaining compliance risk registers and reporting dashboards
  • Coordinating regulatory reporting obligations and compliance submissions
  • Monitoring legislative and regulatory changes and implementing required business improvements
  • Managing relationships with external regulatory bodies, advisors and service providers
  • Supporting governance activities including corporate records, statutory reporting and company administration
  • Developing and delivering compliance training across the organisation
  • Supporting investigations, compliance reviews and corrective actions where required
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Previous experience in a compliance, governance, risk, legal, regulatory or trade compliance position
  • Strong understanding of regulatory frameworks and corporate compliance obligations
  • Experience conducting internal audits, compliance monitoring or assurance reviews
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret legislation, regulations and policy requirements
  • High attention to detail and strong organisational skills
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills
Highly regarded:
  • Experience with import/export controls, trade compliance or customs requirements
  • Exposure to defence, aerospace, manufacturing, logistics, government or other highly regulated industries
  • Tertiary qualifications in Business, Commerce, Law, Governance or a related discipline
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain an Australian Government Security Clearance
  • What's on Offer
  • Hybrid working arrangements
  • 9-day fortnight
  • Brisbane inner northern suburbs location
  • Career development and ongoing professional training
  • Opportunity to work within a highly specialised and regulated environment
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture
  • Long-term career opportunity with a stable organisation

If you are a compliance professional looking to take the next step in your career and enjoy working in a role that combines governance, compliance, risk and stakeholder engagement, we'd love to hear from you.

If interested, please send an updated Resume to Peta McClure at Chandler Macleod using the Apply button.

job.title: Senior Enterprise Agreement / HR specialist
job.description:
About the company:

This is a unique opportunity to join a newly established national public health organisation with a critical role in protecting and improving the health and wellbeing of Australians. As the organisation continues to grow and evolve, there is a strong focus on building a high-performing, inclusive, and values-driven workforce capable of delivering meaningful outcomes for the Australian community.


About the Team

The People and Culture team partners with leaders across the organisation to attract, develop and support a capable workforce. The team provides strategic and operational HR services, workforce planning, industrial and employee relations advice, organisational development, workforce reporting, and people-focused initiatives that help shape the culture and future direction of the organisation.
This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in building and strengthening the people function of a growing agency.

About the Role
As a trusted HR advisor, you will lead key workforce initiatives, provide expert industrial relations guidance, and partner with senior leaders to support organisational goals.
You will be joining an environment that is still evolving, making this an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys building frameworks, improving processes, and driving positive change
 
Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead enterprise agreement bargaining activities, including consultation, stakeholder engagement, implementation, and ongoing support.
  • Provide expert advice on complex industrial and employee relations matters.
  • Use workforce data and insights to support business planning and executive decision-making.
  • Develop and improve HR policies, procedures, and workforce practices.
  • Champion employee engagement, diversity, inclusion, and workplace culture initiatives.
  • Provide advice on employment legislation, APS employment frameworks, and HR policy matters.
  • Lead HR projects and organisational change initiatives.
  • Partner with senior leaders to ensure workforce considerations are integrated into business decisions.
  • Support the ongoing development of a high-performing and values-driven workplace.
 
You Must Have

 
  • Significant experience across strategic and operational human resources functions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading or supporting enterprise bargaining processes and managing complex industrial relations matters.
  • Strong knowledge of employment legislation, industrial instruments, and public sector employment frameworks.
  • Experience providing advice to senior leaders on complex workforce, employee relations, and organisational issues.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
  • Proven experience leading HR projects, workforce initiatives, or organisational change programs.
  • Ability to analyse workforce data and provide practical recommendations to support business outcomes.
  • Strong judgement, problem-solving capability, and decision-making skills.
  • High levels of professionalism, integrity, and discretion when handling sensitive matters.
  • Experience leading, coaching, or mentoring HR professionals is highly regarded.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Organisational Development, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, Law, or a related discipline.
  • Extensive experience in strategic workforce management, industrial relations, or senior HR leadership roles will also be considered in place of formal qualifications.
  • Qualifications in Human Resources, Business, Organisational Development, or a related field will be highly regarded.
 
 
Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 6- Month assignment
  • Location:  Canberra


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

About the Role
As the Strategic Communications & Transformation Director, you will work within a high-profile strategic communications function responsible for shaping organisational narratives, supporting enterprise-wide transformation programs, and strengthening communications capability across the organisation.
Reporting to a senior executive leader, you will provide expert advice on communication strategies, reputation management, organisational change, media engagement, and stakeholder communications. You will play a critical role in designing and implementing communication frameworks, operating models, and strategic initiatives that support long-term organisational success.
This role requires a highly capable leader who can operate with significant autonomy while managing complex, sensitive, and nationally significant communication activities.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead the development and implementation of strategic communications programs supporting organisational transformation and reform initiatives.
  • Design communication strategies that strengthen reputation, manage risk, and support organisational objectives.
  • Provide high-level advice to senior executives on communications planning, stakeholder engagement, public affairs, and reputation management.
  • Develop and implement operating models that improve communications capability, efficiency, and service delivery.
  • Drive the development of long-term communications and change management roadmaps aligned with organisational priorities.
  • Shape strategic narratives, executive messaging, thought leadership opportunities, and communication frameworks.
  • Identify and manage emerging issues, reputational risks, and complex media matters.
  • Lead the delivery of communication plans supporting large-scale organisational change initiatives.
  • Build productive relationships with executive leaders, business areas, media stakeholders, and external partners.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance communications effectiveness and organisational performance.

About You
To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Extensive experience leading strategic communications within large, complex organisations.
  • Proven experience supporting major transformation, organisational change, and reform programs.
  • Strong capability in reputation management, media relations, stakeholder engagement, and public affairs.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop strategic narratives and executive communication frameworks.
  • Experience designing or implementing operating models, governance frameworks, and communication functions.
  • Exceptional communication, influencing, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
  • Strong judgement and decision-making capability in sensitive or high-profile environments.
  • Ability to deliver outcomes within politically sensitive and complex operational environments.
  • Experience advising senior executives and leading multidisciplinary communications teams.

Highly Desirable
  • Experience working within government, public sector, regulatory, media, or highly regulated environments.
  • Significant experience in strategic communications, change communications, media, public affairs, and reputation management.
  • Experience leading organisational design, operating model development, or business transformation initiatives.
  • Demonstrated success supporting major organisational reform programs.
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder environments and high-profile reputational issues.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Corporate Affairs, Marketing, Business, or a related discipline.

Benefits
  • 12-month contract opportunity with potential extension
  • $773.25 per day + Super
  • Surry Hills, NSW

Eligibility:
Australian Citizenship is mandatory for this opportunity. If you are a senior communications leader with a strong background in organisational transformation, strategic communications, media, and reputation management, we encourage you to APPLY NOW.

job.title: Families and Programs Visitor Engagement Officers
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with the Australian National Maritime Museum to find energetic, creative and people-focused Families & Programs Visitor Engagement Officers to join the team in Pyrmont, NSW. 

These casual roles offer varied shifts over an initial three-month engagement, with the possibility of extension. More importantly, they are an opportunity to work at one of Sydney’s most iconic cultural institutions, where no two days are quite the same and you can make a genuine difference to a visitor’s experience. 

ABOUT THE MUSEUM 

The Australian National Maritime Museum is one of the world’s leading maritime museums, welcoming more than 2.5 million visitors each year. Set on Sydney’s waterfront, the Museum is a vibrant, inclusive and engaging place that brings stories to life and creates opportunities for discovery, learning and connection. 

ABOUT THE ROLE 

$33.05-$33.85 PER HOUR + SUPER 

This is not a role where you will simply watch from the sidelines. You will be right at the heart of the visitor experience. 

You will bring creativity, warmth and energy to family programs, activities and public events, helping children aged 0-14 and their carers explore, create, discover and have fun together. 

One day you might be facilitating a hands-on art or science activity in Kids on Deck or Mini Mariners. Another could see you supporting a creative workshop, underwater drone program, guided tour, Sensory Friendly day, performance or major Museum event. 

It is varied, hands-on and people-focused work, with the opportunity to create memorable experiences for families and visitors every day. 

WHAT'S ON OFFER? 

  • Flexible casual rostering to fit around your other commitments 
  • Training and development opportunities 
  • Staff wellbeing initiatives and sailing events 
  • A workplace that genuinely values diversity, inclusion and accessibility 
  • Penalty rates on Sundays and public holidays 
  • The chance to work in an extraordinary waterfront environment and be part of the experiences that bring the Museum to life 
WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

We are looking for people who genuinely enjoy engaging with others and know how to turn an activity, conversation or visit into a great experience. 

YOU'LL BRING: 

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills and confidence engaging with children, families and excursion groups 
  • Experience delivering engaging public programs in a museum or cultural setting 
  • Flexibility and adaptability to work across different activities, programs and environments 
  • Initiative and practical problem-solving skills, particularly when responding to visitor needs 
  • A genuine commitment to excellent customer service and the Museum’s values 
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to contribute to a positive and inclusive team 
  • Experience working with children and families, or studies in Early Childhood or Primary Education 
APPLICATIONS CLOSE AT 11.59 PM ON WEDNESDAY 25 NOVEMBER 2026. 

Please submit your resume and a short cover letter responding to the selection criteria by clicking APPLY. 

Australian citizenship is not required for these positions, as the role is engaged through a labour hire arrangement.

For more information, contact Gary Ward at Chandler Macleod on 02 7245 5361.
